Execution, ownership and the interpreter: Record wall time and CPU utilization for both workloads with one and four threads; distinguish measured native parallelism from Python bytecode execution.
Structured concurrency and backpressure: The heartbeat detects the introduced blocking interval; all tasks finish or cancel within the shared 200 ms budget plus a documented cleanup allowance.
Processes, virtual memory and resource l: Descriptor exhaustion and memory-limit termination are reproduced separately; the supervisor reports each cause and cleans up the disposable workload.
Diagnosing blocked work on Linux: A captured stack or syscall trace identifies the contended lock and the owning thread; the proposed change reduces measured waiting time.
TCP, DNS, TLS and connection budgets: A phase-timing report distinguishes injected DNS delay from read delay and shows the shared deadline prevents their budgets from accumulating.
HTTP semantics, proxies and safe retries: Response loss after commit followed by a retry produces one effect; reusing the key with changed payload returns a documented conflict.
Authentication is not object authorizati: A queued export created before membership revocation fails authorization at execution time and exposes no document bytes.
Tokens, sessions and downstream trust: Old and new signing keys overlap during the rotation window; unknown keys fail closed and no request accepts a token for the wrong audience.
Constraints, isolation and write anomali: Under a barrier-controlled conflict, the serializable implementation retries the complete transaction within a bounded attempt count and preserves stock.
Schema evolution and transaction boundar: A stalled payment dependency does not hold an open business transaction; restart reconciles pending intents without double charging the mock ledger.
Plans, indexes and cardinality: Before/after plans quantify row-estimate error for correlated predicates and explain whether extended statistics changed the chosen plan.
MVCC, vacuum, WAL and connection pools: After a controlled crash, every acknowledged transaction required by the declared durability policy is present; recovery log timestamps are retained.
Partial failure, clocks and consistency: The partition experiment records availability and divergent state for both policies and states how reconciliation resolves conflicting writes.
Retries, idempotency and coordination: A resumed stale lease holder is rejected by the protected resource using an older fencing token; the current holder still completes its write.
Cache-aside, invalidation and stale data: Negative entries stop masking a newly created object within the declared freshness window; revoked access cannot use a cached tenant result.
Stampedes, queueing and measurement: Stale responses never exceed the declared maximum age and at most one refresh per key occupies the bounded refresh queue.
Acknowledgements, duplicates and the out: Business commits succeed while the broker is unavailable; after recovery every committed outbox event reaches the deduplicating projection.
Ordering, retries and long-running jobs: A missing sequence number prevents out-of-order mutation for the affected account while unrelated accounts continue; reconciliation resumes the blocked account.
SLIs, SLOs and overload control: Failure of the optional recommendation dependency leaves reservation correctness intact; overload rejections are bounded and included in the declared SLI.
Metrics, traces and useful logs: A broken propagation link becomes visible in a trace review; request identifiers are removed from metric labels and the resulting series count is bounded.
Properties, contracts and realistic test: The offline contract test fails on the incompatible fixture and passes on the supported shape without making any network request.
Profiling, load shape and capacity: At tenfold payload size, the report repeats throughput, p99, memory and error measurements and identifies whether the limiting resource changed.
Reproducible builds, releases and recove: The isolated restore verifies reservation and job invariants and records elapsed restore time and the newest recoverable transaction timestamp.
Architecture, system design and engineer: The regional recovery plan declares numerical RPO/RTO targets and one local component drill measures achieved recovery against those targets.
Consensus and replicated state machines: Duplicate client commands appear once in the applied state despite multiple log entries or retries; the report separates this rule from Raft log agreement.
Storage engines and recovery contracts: Each batch configuration records throughput, acknowledgement latency and the maximum acknowledged-data loss allowed by its flush policy.
Scheduling, autoscaling and platform bou: The Azure alternative names managed versus application responsibilities and estimates monthly cost using explicit traffic, storage and availability assumptions.
Threat models and secure operations: The review removes one unnecessary container capability or dependency permission and reruns the relevant abuse fixture to prove required behavior still works.
Contention, batching and memory costs: Streaming input reduces or explains the absence of a reduction in peak allocation; end-to-end throughput and p99 are compared with the original pipeline.
Events, projections and semantic version: Historical event fixtures rebuild both projections from zero; schema-version changes preserve the meaning of older records without editing history.
Tokens, attention and next-token predict: At least five minimal prompt pairs change one fact only; the report records when output follows the changed evidence and when it ignores it.
Decoding, inference cost and uncertainty: Context-length experiments hold model, settings and output budget constant and report TTFT, completion latency and memory where observable.
Typed requests and validated results: Schema-valid but impossible dates and out-of-range amounts are rejected as semantic errors with no downstream tool effect.
Streaming is an event protocol: Cancellation closes the stream and marks the turn incomplete; tool argument buffers exceeding the configured byte limit are rejected before execution.
Schemas are contracts, tool calls are pr: Deeply nested and oversized payloads are rejected within a declared input-size/depth limit before expensive tool work or unbounded allocation.
Dispatch, permissions and execution budg: A write that times out after commit enters an uncertain/reconciliation state and is not automatically repeated by the dispatcher.
The agent is a state machine: Malformed actions terminate with a typed error; repeated identical tool cycles stop at the configured repetition or step limit with the trace intact.
Context is a budgeted working set: Every summary references original event IDs; the same task set compares success and retained constraints before and after compression.
Hosts, clients, servers and protocol rev: Revision-labeled fixtures retain separate handshake and per-request metadata paths; unsupported combinations fail with explicit version errors.
Transport, tool discovery and authentica: Expired credentials and metadata/header mismatch produce distinct failures; tokens do not appear in traces, errors or persisted run events.
Event history, checkpoints and replay: The injected post-effect crash resumes into a deduplicated result or explicit operator reconciliation; no unacknowledged second write occurs.
Workflows before open-ended autonomy: The LangGraph comparison runs the same crash and approval fixtures and documents where replay reuses recorded output versus re-executing a tool.
Indexing, chunking and retrieval evaluat: The chunking comparison keeps queries and corpus revision fixed and reports recall@5 plus at least five changed relevance judgments.
Hybrid search, reranking and grounded ge: Unanswerable queries are scored separately; the system abstains without fabricating a citation and reports false-answer and false-abstention counts.
History, working memory and long-term re: Expired and deleted memory records are absent from both search results and subsequent prompt context, including previously cached candidate lists.
Artifacts, hydration and consistency: The reconciliation job finds the deliberately orphaned blob and applies the documented retain/delete policy without deleting a referenced live artifact.
Datasets, scorers and experimental disci: The human/model-judge comparison reports agreement and the actual disagreement cases; no judge sees hidden reference labels in its candidate prompt.
Stochasticity, replay and adversarial re: Each minimized fixture reproduces its original failure offline and fails when the relevant guard is deliberately removed.
Prompt injection and the confused deputy: Changing approved normalized arguments invalidates the approval; the mutated operation never reaches the tool implementation.
Sandbox boundaries and credential scope: The sandbox cannot read broker credentials or request a resource outside the tool-specific scope; audit records identify each denied attempt without exposing secrets.
Tracing runs and controlling cost: A synthetic canary secret appears in no exported log, span or evaluation artifact; automated scanning reports the checked artifact set.
Latency budgets, routing and graceful fa: The routing comparison reports total cost including retries/escalations, task success and p95 latency on the same held-out inputs.
Designing the harness boundaries: Replacing one adapter leaves the loop unchanged and passes the same provider/persistence contract fixtures, including cancellation and recovery cases.
Release review and framework comparison: A cold-start review completes setup and one failure-recovery drill from the runbook alone; missing steps become corrected documentation and regression checks.
Coordination, handoffs and shared state: A malicious child message cannot expand tool scopes or alter the root user goal; the supervisor records the rejected instruction and preserves evidence.
Retrieval planning and temporal truth: The two-hop planner uses no more than the declared retrieval budget and every intermediate inference cites a retrieved source passage.
Quantization, batching and KV memory: Requests exceeding the configured context or admission limit are rejected before allocation; admitted requests remain within the declared memory budget.
Media content blocks and evidence: The labeled small-text comparison reports exact-match errors by preprocessing variant and preserves original source identity for every resized image.
Isolation as defense in depth: The credential broker rejects requests for another resource or principal; runner code cannot obtain the broker’s underlying credential material.
Training objectives, LoRA and data quali: The distribution-shift suite compares baseline and adapted models using held-out sources and reports regressions as well as target-task gains.
Evaluation as a production data pipeline: The paired comparison reports a bootstrap interval with resampling method and seed, plus separate counts of critical policy violations.
